facts.fact_text: The case concerns restrictions of the applicant's rights to take part in a public event, under Article 11 of the Convention.
The applicant planned to hold a demonstration.
On 27 March 2009, the Deputy Prefect of the Central Administrative District of Moscow again refused to authorise the picket.
The picket organisers decided to cancel the event that they had planned.
The Taganskiy District Court of Moscow referred to the definition of a public event as specified by section 2(1) of the Public Events Act (no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004).

Under section 2(1) of the Public Events Act (no. FZ-54 of 19 June 2004), a public event was one which aimed to express or develop opinions freely and to voice demands on issues related to political, economic, social or cultural life in the country, or issues related to foreign policy.

The Deputy Prefect of the Central Administrative District of Moscow noted that the statistics provided by the applicant and the two other picket organisers were not in line with the relevant data from the Ministry of Health and Social Development of the Russian Federation.

The Taganskiy District Court of Moscow held that since the picket at issue did not pursue any aims related to expressing or developing opinions freely or voicing demands on issues related to political, economic, social or cultural life in the country, or issues related to foreign policy, the refusals to authorise it had been lawful.
